title: log4net
description: log4net is a port of the popular Java logging framework log4j. It provides flexible logging with configurable appenders and layouts.

data.text: log4net is a proven logging library that has been used in .NET for over a decade. It follows a similar model to log4j, where you configure appenders (where logs go) and layouts (how logs look) through an XML configuration file.

data.title: Basic log4net Setup
data.content: Configure log4net programmatically with a console appender.

terms.definition: A destination that writes log events, such as ConsoleAppender, FileAppender, or AdoNetAppender.
Controls how each log event is formatted, using patterns like %date, %level, and %message.
The entry point for logging. Obtain one with LogManager.GetLogger(typeof(MyClass)).

data.title: XML Configuration
data.text: Most log4net users configure appenders via log4net.config XML. The programmatic approach shown here is useful for understanding the underlying model.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: log4net uses appenders and layouts to control log output
It is mature and widely used in legacy .NET applications
XML configuration is the most common setup method
data.takeaway: log4net remains a solid choice, especially when maintaining existing applications.

data.title: Exercise: Add a File Appender
data.description: Extend the basic log4net setup to also write logs to a file.
steps: Create a new console project and install log4net
Add a FileAppender alongside the ConsoleAppender
Set the file path to app.log
Log a mix of Info, Warn, and Error messages
Verify both the console and the log file contain the expected entries
data.expectedOutcome: Both console and file outputs receive the same log events.
